docs.title: Your Matrix server. Your administration.
docs.text:
Whistor deploys a Matrix/Synapse messaging server with a Tor v3 hidden service and a web interface to manage users from your own PC.

Install Whistor Manage users

docs.title: Two tasks, two access paths
docs.text:
Task On your PC On the server Chat on Matrix A Tor-compatible client such as element-tor Synapse and Tor Manage accounts A browser over LAN, Tailscale or an SSH tunnel The Docker admin service on port 8080

Open the browser on your PC, not on the machine hosting Whistor. Sign in to the administration interface with a Synapse administrator account. Your Linux/SSH account is separate.

docs.title: What you can manage
docs.text:
• Create, search and edit users.
  • Reset passwords and assign administrator privileges.
  • Deactivate accounts that should no longer have access.
  • Use the additional tools provided by Ketesa, the integrated administration interface.

Federation and public registration are disabled by default. Message encryption depends on end-to-end encryption being enabled in your Matrix clients.

Network scope

The .onion service remains available for Matrix. The administration service also exposes Synapse's client and administrator APIs on its configured network address. The entire deployment should therefore not be considered Tor-only. Read the architecture guide to choose your access model.

docs.title: Resources
docs.text:
• Whistor source code
  • Download element-tor
  • IT-Projects catalogue

Documentation checked on November 17, 2026, with Synapse latest and the integrated administration service. Images tagged latest change over time: review upstream release notes before upgrading.

docs.title: Choose your access method
docs.text: Method Open on your PC Requirements LAN, without a VPN http://SERVER_LAN_IP:8080 Same network or LAN routing; firewall allowing TCP 8080 Direct Tailscale http://SERVER_TAILSCALE_IP:8080 Both devices on the same tailnet; policy allowing TCP 8080 Tailscale Serve HTTPS URL printed by Tailscale Serve/HTTPS enabled for your tailnet SSH http://localhost:8080 after opening a tunnel SSH access to the server Internet without a VPN Your HTTPS domain An HTTPS reverse proxy on the server

docs.title: LAN: the direct route
docs.text:
The service listens on 0.0.0.0:8080 by default. On your PC, open http://192.168.1.42:8080, replacing the example address with your server's IP. No Matrix proxy or Tor configuration is needed for administration.

Your server firewall and network rules must allow the connection. Allow the networks you intend to use; Whistor does not modify your firewall automatically.

docs.title: Direct Tailscale access
docs.text:
Install Tailscale on both the server and your PC, join the same tailnet, then check the server's address:

tailscale ip -4

On your PC, open http://THE_PRINTED_ADDRESS:8080. Tailnet policies must allow your PC to reach that port. No public port forwarding on your router is required.

docs.title: Tailscale Serve with HTTPS
docs.text:
On the server:

tailscale serve --bg http://127.0.0.1:8080
tailscale serve status

Open the printed HTTPS URL from your PC connected to the tailnet. Tailscale may ask you to enable Serve and HTTPS. This uses Serve, not Funnel: access stays private to your tailnet.

For access exclusively through this method, set WHISTOR_ADMIN_BIND=127.0.0.1 in .env and recreate the service.

docs.title: SSH tunnel
docs.text:
Run this on your PC and keep the terminal open:

ssh -N -L 8080:127.0.0.1:8080 USER@SERVER

Then open http://localhost:8080. If your local port is already in use:

ssh -N -L 18080:127.0.0.1:8080 USER@SERVER

In that case, open http://localhost:18080 in your browser.

docs.title: Change the port or bind address
docs.text:
In .env, next to docker-compose.yml:

WHISTOR_ADMIN_BIND=0.0.0.0
WHISTOR_ADMIN_PORT=8080
Bind address Effect 0.0.0.0 All IPv4 interfaces, including LAN and Tailscale Server's LAN IP Only that interface Server's Tailscale IP Only that interface; it must exist when the service starts 127.0.0.1 Local access, SSH, Tailscale Serve or a local reverse proxy

Apply changes on the server:

docker compose up -d --build admin

Update your URLs and tunnel commands if you change the port.

docs.title: Manage accounts
docs.text:
1. Sign in with a Synapse administrator account, separate from your Linux login.
  2. Search for an account in the users list or create a new one.
  3. Change its display name, password or privileges as needed.
  4. Deactivate an account to remove access. Deactivation does not automatically mean that all associated data is erased.
  5. Keep at least one working administrator and sign out when finished.

Synapse checks permissions: an ordinary user cannot call the administration APIs, even if they can open the login page.

docs.title: Internet access without a VPN
docs.text:
Put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of http://127.0.0.1:8080. Use a dedicated hostname at /, preserve the Host header and send X-Forwarded-Proto: https. Deploying under a URL subpath is not supported.

Do not send administrator credentials over the Internet using HTTP; use HTTPS. Publishing this proxy also makes the relayed Matrix APIs reachable at that address. Choose network access rules accordingly.

docs.title: Three services
docs.text:
Tor-compatible Matrix client
    → Tor network → .onion:8448 service → synapse:8008

Browser on your PC (LAN / Tailscale / SSH)
    → server:8080 → admin (Ketesa + Nginx) → synapse:8008
Service Purpose Docker networks synapse Matrix homeserver and SQLite database matrix-internal tor Hidden service and .onion identity matrix-internal, tor-external admin Web interface and Synapse API proxy matrix-internal, admin-access

Only admin publishes a server port. Synapse does not directly publish a host port. The browser uses the same origin for the interface and Matrix requests: it does not need to resolve synapse, which is an internal Docker hostname.

docs.title: Access model
docs.text:
• The interface is reachable on your chosen network. Synapse authenticates the administrator account and checks permissions on API requests.
  • The proxy forwards /_matrix/ and /_synapse/ to Synapse. Publishing the administration port also exposes these routes.
  • The administration container cannot access the Docker socket, Tor keys or Synapse data volume. Its root filesystem is read-only, with in-memory temporary directories.
  • Federation and public registration are disabled by the default configuration. This does not replace authentication or firewall rules.
  • GitHub Pages hosts only this public documentation. It does not host your administration instance, passwords or private keys.

docs.title: Choose your exposure
docs.text: Use your server's LAN address for local access. For private remote access, choose direct Tailscale or Tailscale Serve. For remote access without a VPN, place an HTTPS reverse proxy in front of the service. Variables in .env select the interface and port without editing the Compose file.

docs.title: Connect a Matrix client
docs.text: The administration interface on :8080 manages your server. For messaging over Tor, use your .onion homeserver address.

docs.title: Find the homeserver address
docs.text:
On the server, from the Whistor checkout:

export WHISTOR_DIR="$PWD"
./whistor onion

The URL has this format:

http://YOUR_ADDRESS.onion:8448

Local Matrix user IDs look like @alice:YOUR_ADDRESS.onion.

docs.title: Desktop: element-tor
docs.text:
Download the package for your platform from the element-tor releases. Release V-Tor.1.1 is based on Element 1.12.35 and provides:

Platform Package Linux x86_64 AppImage Windows x64 MSI macOS Intel x64 DMG or ZIP macOS Apple Silicon arm64 DMG or ZIP

Launch the application and wait for Tor to connect. On the login screen, replace the suggested server with your .onion URL, then sign in with your Matrix account.

Calls

The fork blocks attempts to open Element Call: WebRTC/UDP is not carried by the Tor proxy. Do not expect the audio/video calling features of a standard client to work in this setup.

docs.title: Other clients and mobile
docs.text:
A client must be able to reach and resolve your .onion address through Tor. On Android, Orbot's VPN mode is an option depending on the client. On iOS, availability depends on the client and operating system limitations.

Do not assume that a standard Element client includes compatible SOCKS5 settings. Check the features of the version you use. Choose element-tor on Desktop if you want the fork's integrated proxy.

docs.title: Check your first conversation
docs.text: Create a second account through the administration interface, sign in with it from another client and start a conversation. Enable end-to-end encryption as needed, verify your devices and retain your key recovery information. Server backups do not replace client encryption key backups.

docs.title: Prepare your server
docs.text:
Use a Linux server with Docker and the Docker Compose v2 plugin. Debian and Ubuntu are suitable choices. Allow at least 1 GB of RAM and 10 GB of storage, with more capacity for additional users and media.

Your account must be able to run Docker. The server needs connectivity to download images and join the Tor network. Your administration PC needs access to the server over LAN, Tailscale or SSH.

docker --version
docker compose version
git --version

docs.title: Deploy from Git
docs.text:
On the server:

git clone https://github.com/Gvte-Kali/Whistor.git
cd Whistor
export WHISTOR_DIR="$PWD"
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up -d --build

The default configuration publishes administration on all IPv4 interfaces, port 8080. Edit .env before starting if you want a different bind address or port. See access options.

Run the CLI from your checkout

These guides use ./whistor. Keep WHISTOR_DIR set to your checkout's absolute path in the current shell. After reconnecting over SSH, return to that directory and run export WHISTOR_DIR="$PWD" again. This avoids relying on the installed CLI's default directory.

docs.title: Check the first startup
docs.text:
docker compose ps
docker compose logs --tail=50 tor synapse admin
./whistor onion

Tor creates the .onion identity in its volume. Synapse waits for that hostname before generating configuration and secrets. The first startup can take several minutes. Do not delete volumes to speed it up.

docs.title: Create your administrator
docs.text:
Once Synapse is running:

./whistor user admin myadmin

Enter a password at the prompt. If you already have an administrator, use the existing account instead of recreating it.

On your PC, open http://SERVER_IP:8080 and sign in with this account. The interface detects the homeserver automatically.

Configure LAN or Tailscale access

docs.title: Automated installer
docs.text:
The repository also provides install.sh. It downloads the project files, builds the administration service and installs the CLI when permissions allow it. To review the script before executing it:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Gvte-Kali/Whistor/main/install.sh -o install.sh
less install.sh
bash install.sh

Check the installation directory printed by the script and set WHISTOR_DIR if your CLI points elsewhere. The Git method above is recommended for a reproducible checkout and future source updates.

docs.title: Understand latest
docs.text:
Synapse uses ghcr.io/element-hq/synapse:latest. The administration image is built from Ketesa latest and Nginx stable-alpine. Versions change over time; an upgrade may include database migrations.

Before updating, review the Synapse upgrade notes, including the notes for every intermediate version you skip.

docs.title: Back up your deployment
docs.text:
Keep these items:

Item Why it matters tor-data volume Private keys and the .onion identity synapse-data volume Database, configuration, media and signing key .env and deployment files Network settings and reproducible configuration

Volume names usually include the Compose project prefix. Check them with docker volume ls; do not assume they always start with whistor_.

For a consistent SQLite backup, stop services that write data before archiving. From your deployment directory on the server:

mkdir -p backups
docker compose stop synapse tor admin
docker compose run --rm --no-deps --user 0 --entrypoint /bin/sh \
  -v "$PWD/backups:/backup" synapse \
  -c 'tar -czf /backup/whistor-data.tar.gz -C /data .'
docker compose run --rm --no-deps --user 0 --entrypoint /bin/sh \
  -v "$PWD/backups:/backup" tor \
  -c 'tar -czf /backup/whistor-tor.tar.gz -C /var/lib/tor/hidden_service .'
docker compose up -d

These commands overwrite the two archives if they already exist. Move each backup to a dated directory before creating another. Also copy .env and record the checkout commit (git rev-parse HEAD) and image references (docker compose images). Keep a restricted-access copy off the server.

The ./whistor backup command is also available, but uses predefined volume names and does not pause Synapse. Check those assumptions before relying on it for a critical backup.

docs.title: Update the source and images
docs.text:
On the server, after backing up:

cd /path/to/Whistor
export WHISTOR_DIR="$PWD"
git pull --ff-only
./whistor update

whistor update pulls Synapse and Tor images, rebuilds administration with the latest base images, then recreates containers. It does not run git pull for you. Afterwards, check docker compose ps, logs and a test login from your PC.

docs.title: Restore
docs.text:
Restore into an isolated environment first when possible. Use images and source matching your backup. Stop services, then restore each archive to its corresponding volume, preserving ownership and permissions. Restore .env before restarting.

Do not start an older Synapse version on a database migrated by a newer version: rolling back also requires the matching data backup. Do not run docker compose down -v on your deployment to troubleshoot an incident. It deletes volumes and can permanently destroy your .onion identity.

docs.title: The page does not open from my PC
docs.text:
On the server:

docker compose ps
docker compose logs --tail=50 admin
docker compose port admin 8080
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/health

Adjust the URL to your configured bind address and port. 127.0.0.1 in your PC's browser refers to your PC, not the server, unless an SSH tunnel is active. Then check your firewall, LAN routing or Tailscale policies.

With WHISTOR_ADMIN_BIND=127.0.0.1, use SSH/Tailscale Serve, or choose a LAN/Tailscale address in .env and recreate admin.

docs.title: The page loads, but Synapse does not respond
docs.text:
docker compose logs --tail=100 synapse tor
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/_matrix/client/versions

The static interface can become available before Synapse finishes starting. On first startup, check that Tor has generated the expected hostname and that volumes are shared correctly. A 502 error can also mean Synapse is stopped or cannot be resolved from the internal Docker network.

docs.title: Login fails or permissions are missing
docs.text:
Use a Synapse administrator account, not your SSH password. An ordinary Matrix account cannot manage users. To create an administrator:

export WHISTOR_DIR="$PWD"
./whistor user admin newadmin

Avoid editing SQLite directly while Synapse is running. If that username already exists, choose another name or use an existing administrator to grant it privileges.

docs.title: Tailscale works, but the interface does not
docs.text: Check that both devices are on the same tailnet, that the server listens on its Tailscale IP or 0.0.0.0, and that your policies allow TCP 8080. With Serve, use tailscale serve status and the printed HTTPS URL. If you change the Docker port, update Serve's target as well.

docs.title: A port is already in use
docs.text:
Change WHISTOR_ADMIN_PORT in .env, then run:

docker compose up -d --build admin

For SSH, you can choose a different local port such as 18080 while keeping 8080 on the server.

docs.title: The CLI uses the wrong directory
docs.text:
From the directory containing docker-compose.yml:

export WHISTOR_DIR="$PWD"
./whistor admin

This overrides the default directory used by some CLI installations.

docs.title: Problems after an update
docs.text: Check logs, Synapse upgrade notes and your backup. Do not delete volumes. See maintenance before restoring. When reporting a problem on GitHub, include your Docker version, checkout commit and logs with credentials, tokens, secrets and private keys removed.
